summary.text: A six months old girl presented with a right orbital swelling increasing over two months; examination found a roughly 5 x 4 cm firm, non-tender right orbitotemporal swelling. CT without contrast showed a soft tissue swelling with hyperdense bone overgrowth and bony spurs; MRI was not done and the initial diagnosis was osteoma.

Hyperostotic bone was completely excised through a single burr hole, the dura was coagulated and closure was done without cranioplasty, without intraoperative complications; postoperative CT showed complete resection. Histopathology showed a biphasic cell population with melanin pigmentation and confirmed MNTI; immunohistochemistry was not done.
At six months of follow-up she was asymptomatic with no cosmetic disfigurement, complications or tumor regrowth and normal milestones.

summary.text: A three-month-old boy (5.8 kg) presented with a rapidly growing right temporal scalp swelling over three weeks; examination found a 3 x 2 cm firm, non-tender, non-pulsatile swelling attached to underlying structures.

CT showed a well-defined extra-axial lesion with right temporal bone and sphenoid hyperostosis, sylvian fissure obliteration and temporal lobe compression; MRI showed an extra-axial lesion with avid contrast enhancement, dural attachment and hyperostosis. The differentials were meningioma and fibrous dysplasia.

Wide local excision removed thickened bone and soft tissue without intraoperative complications and without cranioplasty. Histopathology showed a biphasic cell population with melanin pigment and confirmed MNTI; immunohistochemistry was not done. At six months of follow-up he was doing fine with no recurrence or complications and normal milestones.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; actual images are reviewed in the separate visual record.
MNTI is described in the abstract as mostly benign in nature; it is recorded as a confirmed condition and not as an oncology tumor entry.
The two cases are treated between April and May 2024 with a gap of one month; no calendar time is assigned to either patient.
Fig.4 caption (g) describes the T2-weighted coronal lesion as hypointense whereas the main text says hyperintense on T2; both are kept as source conflict, review-only facts for patient 2.

The discussion states urinary VMA was not done in our case (singular) and that neuroblastoma and rhabdomyosarcoma were ruled out on history and examination, without naming a patient; neither is recorded as a patient fact.
Discussion and literature-review text is background and not copied to the patients, except statements that explicitly cover both patients (immunohistochemistry not done, disease-free follow-up).

The abstract states that CT and MRI in both cases showed extra-axial lesions, whereas the case 1 report says MRI was not done; case 1 keeps MRI as not performed and no extra-axial finding is recorded for case 1.
